subject: microbiology
title: Negri Bodies, Rabies PEP, Ebola, Hantavirus and CCHF

steps.tx: **Negri bodies** are eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in neurons infected by rabies virus, classically in hippocampal pyramidal cells and Purkinje cells. They supported historical postmortem diagnosis but are neither universally present nor as sensitive as direct fluorescent antibody testing or PCR. Their absence cannot clear an animal or human specimen. Corneal impression tests are obsolete and should not delay exposure management.
steps.say: Negri bodies are historic clues; modern rabies diagnosis usesFAT and molecular tests.

left.title: Negri body facts
points: Contain rabies viral antigen and RNA
Can be absent in confirmed rabies

right.title: Modern diagnosis
points: RT-PCR on saliva, CSF or skin biopsy
Nuchal skin biopsy can help antemortem
No test result should delay indicated PEP

steps.tx: **Post-exposure prophylaxis** works because rabies incubation is usually long enough for vaccine-induced antibody to intercept virus before central nervous system entry. Wash wounds for at least fifteen minutes, avoid suturing initially, infiltrate immunoglobulin into and around category III wounds, and vaccinate into deltoid. Previously vaccinated people receive shorter vaccine courses and no immunoglobulin.
steps.say: PEP succeeds by winning a race against slow axonal transport.

left.title: Unvaccinated severe exposure
points: Tetanus and bacterial wound care also needed

steps.tx: **Ebola virus** is a filovirus causing severe haemorrhagic fever with fever, vomiting, diarrhoea, fluid loss, shock and coagulopathy after contact with blood or body fluids of patients or bodies. It is not casually airborne in ordinary care, but aerosol-generating and sharps procedures raise risk. Early isolation, meticulous PPE, safe fluids and electrolyte care and safe burials interrupt outbreaks.
steps.say: Ebola spreads through body-fluid contact, so barrier discipline and safe burial save lives.

left.title: Transmission
points: Blood, vomit, diarrhoea and other fluids
Contaminated sharps and surfaces while wet
Sexual persistence in survivors can occur rarely

steps.tx: **Hantaviruses** are rodent-borne RNA viruses causing haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome in the Americas. Exposure follows inhaling aerosolised rodent urine or droppings in sheds, homes or fields. Thrombocytopenia, haemoconcentration and capillary leak dominate; treatment is supportive, with ventilatory and renal care deciding outcome.
steps.say: Rodent excreta aerosols connect hantavirus fever to renal or pulmonary capillary leak.

left.title: Old World pattern
points: Hantaan, Seoul, Puumala and Dobrava viruses
Milder Puumala disease is nephropathia epidemica
Rodent control and dust avoidance help

right.title: New World pattern
points: Andes virus can transmit person to person rarely

steps.tx: **Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever** is a tick-borne nairovirus also transmitted by livestock blood and nosocomial exposure. Fever, myalgia, thrombocytopenia, hepatitis and haemorrhage progress rapidly in severe cases. Ribavirin is often used although evidence is debated; meticulous barrier nursing and laboratory biosafety are crucial. Virus isolation demands high-containment reference laboratories.
steps.say: CCHF combines tick exposure, livestock blood and high-risk hospital transmission.

right.title: Diagnosis and care
points: Use strict standard and contact precautions

steps.tx: Across viral haemorrhagic fevers the first action is not naming the virus but **isolating the patient, minimising sharps and fluid exposure, notifying public health and sending appropriate PCR safely**. Malaria, dengue, leptospirosis, typhoid and sepsis remain common mimics and may need parallel treatment. A travel, animal, tick and sick-contact history taken in the first minutes shapes the entire pathway.
steps.say: In viral haemorrhagic fever, infection control starts before species confirmation.

nodes.label: Travel, tick, animal and contact history
